freeze.rule: This file is the single authoritative P1-04 storage contract. DEC-011 accepts it. Implementation must not begin until this contract and DEC-011 are merged, and must not diverge from it without a new reviewed decision.
freeze.implementation_state: design-only: at the freeze commit there is no persistence code, no SQLite dependency, no schema migration and no CLI change for reference storage

authority.implementation_evidence: source files, tests and cargo xtask gate evidence
rules: This document freezes design decisions. It does not mark any capability implemented or verified.
Capability states are unchanged by this freeze: INDIA-REF-INGEST is implemented, not verified; INDIA-FNO-INGEST remains proposed.
Where this contract and an older source comment disagree, this contract wins and the source comment must be corrected in the implementation change.

owns: Durable immutable reference revisions that survive process restart with stable revision identity and parent relationships.
A versioned on-disk snapshot payload, its decoding and its validation before callers can observe it.
A semantic snapshot hash and a separate payload-integrity checksum with frozen meanings.
Safe concurrent publication of raw source bytes in the existing SHA-256 content-addressed archive, including a per-root cross-process lock and manifest tail recovery.
Backup and restore of the database together with the source archive, and verification of every source reference after restore.
excludes: NSE F&O ingestion; INDIA-FNO-INGEST remains proposed.
Point-in-time research datasets, Parquet storage and analytics datasets.
Strategy IR, alpha generation and backtesting.
OMS, broker adapters, execution routing and independent risk authority.
Redesign of the account journal or the raw market-data journal.
Postgres, object storage, distributed services, cloud infrastructure and multi-node replication.
Normalizing every instrument and listing into relational SQL tables in this milestone.

claimed: Process crash, process kill and application restart on a local filesystem that honors fsync and directory sync.
OS crash or power loss on local storage that honors SQLite synchronous=FULL semantics and the archive's fsync ordering.
not_claimed: Disk, controller or firmware failure that loses acknowledged writes.
Malicious modification, accidental deletion or filesystem corruption.
Network filesystems, cloud-synced folders or any directory whose sync semantics differ from a local filesystem.
Disaster recovery until backup and restore are executed and verified, not merely documented.
durability_promise.recovery_rule: Reopen, verify durable state and resolve in-flight publications by publication key. Never report success after an unresolved durability failure.

deployment.dependency_rule: The SQLite binding is added only in the implementation change. It must bundle SQLite, support online backup and require no external service.
deployment.data_directory_rule: All durable reference state lives under one configurable application data directory outside the Git working tree. The directory must not be a network filesystem or a cloud-synced folder.

entries.role: revision catalogue, immutable snapshot payloads and the singleton head
append-only commit record for retained raw source bytes
write-once raw source bytes addressed by SHA-256
per-root cross-process advisory lock; never a source object and never a manifest entry
verified database-plus-archive backups; never read by normal operation

field_rules: The field set is exact. Unknown fields are rejected; absent non-optional fields are rejected.
valid_at is the trading date the snapshot describes, encoded as YYYY-MM-DD.
recorded_at is the snapshot knowledge time, encoded as UTC RFC 3339.
provenance describes the raw source file that produced this universe.
instruments is the complete instrument universe in canonical order.
calendar is the carried trading calendar or null.
reconciliation is the reconciliation recorded while building this snapshot or null.
listing_states is the accumulated listing-state history in canonical order; each record keeps its own recorded_at and provenance.

encoding.field_order: declared order of the versioned storage structs
encoding.timestamps: UTC RFC 3339 emitted by the single version-1 storage encoder; the encoder version is frozen with the payload schema and byte identity is authoritative
encoding.integers: JSON numbers, never strings or floats
encoding.authoritative_bytes: The exact encoded bytes are stored and hashed. Verification never re-serializes before comparing.

decoding: Decoding is explicit and versioned; do not reuse a wire schema version as the storage version.
Every payload is decoded, then validated by the domain rules in this contract, before any caller can observe it.
A payload that parses but fails validation is corrupt and is not returned.
The current Serialize-only types require deliberate Deserialize support in the implementation change; deserialization does not replace validation.

columns.name: revision_id
columns.constraints: primary key; >= 0; zero-based and contiguous with no reuse

columns.name: parent_revision_id
columns.constraints: unique; foreign key to reference_revision(revision_id); null only for revision 0; otherwise exactly revision_id - 1

columns.name: payload_schema_version
columns.constraints: not null; must equal the envelope schema_version and the supported payload version

columns.name: valid_at
columns.constraints: not null; canonical YYYY-MM-DD; equals the payload value

columns.name: recorded_at
columns.constraints: not null; canonical UTC RFC 3339; equals the payload value

columns.name: snapshot_hash
columns.constraints: not null; 64 lowercase hex digits; equals recomputation from the decoded payload

columns.name: payload_sha256
columns.constraints: not null; 64 lowercase hex digits; equals SHA-256 of the exact payload bytes

columns.name: publication_key
columns.constraints: not null; unique; 64 lowercase hex digits

columns.name: payload
columns.constraints: not null; exact encoded envelope bytes

checks: revision 0 has no parent; every later revision's parent is revision_id - 1
all hex fields are 64 lowercase hex digits
no other unique constraints or indexes are required until a measured query needs them
immutability: No update or delete operation is exposed for published revisions.
Database triggers abort UPDATE and DELETE on reference_revision.
A correction appends a new revision; it never rewrites an old payload or metadata row.

columns.name: singleton_id
columns.constraints: primary key; exactly 1 when a head exists

columns.name: revision_id
columns.constraints: not null; foreign key to reference_revision(revision_id); equals the highest committed revision

rules: The table contains at most one row.
The head row is inserted and updated only in the same transaction that inserts a revision.
An empty store has no revision rows and no head row.

session_pragmas: journal_mode = WAL, and the returned mode is verified to be wal
busy_timeout = 5000 ms by default, always finite, positive and bounded
all writes use BEGIN IMMEDIATE, never a deferred write transaction

revision_ids.scheme: zero-based contiguous u64, matching the existing publish() contract
revision_ids.allocation: next id equals head + 1, or 0 when the store is empty; allocation happens inside the publication transaction
revision_ids.rule: Published ids are never reused, renumbered or reallocated after a failed or uncertain publication.

preconditions: The snapshot validates under this contract.

Every SHA-256 referenced by the snapshot resolves to a manifest entry and hash-correct retained bytes: top-level provenance, every listing-state provenance, and every monthly tick assignment reference-close, schedule and calendar hash.
The expected parent revision is supplied by the caller; null means the empty store.
protocol: Archive every referenced raw source first and wait for its durable object and manifest entry.
Verify each referenced source object against the archive manifest and its SHA-256.
Compare it with the expected parent revision.
If the publication key already names a committed revision, verify the stored payload and parent, then return the existing revision without inserting or updating the head.
Insert the immutable revision with payload, metadata and publication key.
Insert or update the singleton head to the new revision id.
publication.atomicity: The revision insert and head update succeed or fail together. A crash before commit leaves neither; a successful commit leaves both visible after reopen.

expected_parent.rule: If the current head differs from the expected parent and the publication key does not already name a committed revision, reject with a stale-parent error.
expected_parent.reason: A snapshot reconciled against an older head must never silently overwrite newer knowledge.
expected_parent.empty_store: Expected parent null is valid only when no head exists; expected parent non-null is invalid when the store is empty.

publication_key.input: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the serde_json JSON array [marker, expected_parent_revision_id_or_null, payload_schema_version, payload_sha256], where marker is the string 'p1-04-publication-v1'
publication_key.purpose: A retry of the same publication resolves to the same revision instead of creating a duplicate.
publication_key.conflict_rule: If a stored row has the key but a different parent, payload checksum or payload bytes, fail closed as corruption; never reuse the key for different content.

triggers: COMMIT or the post-commit durability read fails in a way that does not prove the transaction rolled back
the connection reports an I/O, full-disk, protocol or unknown outcome on the commit path
required_behavior: Mark the writer handle poisoned; it refuses all further reads and writes.
Close the connection without claiming success.
Reopen the store and resolve the publication key against durable state.
If the key names a committed revision with the same parent and payload checksum, report that revision id.
If the key is absent, the publication did not commit and may be retried normally.
If the key exists with different content, fail closed as corruption.
uncertain_commit.known_rollback: A commit rejected with a busy result is a known rollback: roll back and retry with bounded backoff; do not poison the handle.

concurrency: SQLite serializes writers across processes; BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus the expected-parent check prevents duplicate or stale publication.
The archive's per-root cross-process lock covers the manifest check, object deduplication and manifest publication.
A publication that loses the race must return stale-parent or resolve by publication key, never a duplicate revision.

semantic_snapshot_hash.input: serde_json::to_vec of an object with exactly the keys valid_at, instruments, calendar and listing_states
included: the complete instruments vector in canonical order
the complete listing_states vector in canonical order, including each record's embedded provenance
excluded: payload_schema_version, payload_sha256 and storage commit metadata
semantic_snapshot_hash.frozen_meaning: This preserves the current snapshot_hash() field meaning. Listing-state provenance is hashed today because it is embedded in the serialized records; the implementation must correct the misleading source comment without changing the bytes.
semantic_snapshot_hash.failure_rule: Serialization failure aborts publication. An empty-input or default-bytes fallback is forbidden.
semantic_snapshot_hash.change_rule: Changing the included fields, canonical order, encoding or algorithm is a semantic change requiring a new payload schema version and a new reviewed decision.

payload_sha256.input: the exact stored payload BLOB bytes, including the envelope
payload_sha256.purpose: storage-integrity checksum covering top-level provenance, reconciliation and every other stored byte
payload_sha256.verification: Recompute over the stored bytes and compare with the column and, on full verification, with the row metadata. Never accept a decoded object whose checksum does not match.

metadata_checks: valid_at and recorded_at columns equal the decoded payload values.
snapshot_hash equals recomputation from the decoded payload on load and on full verification.

canonical_order.instruments: strictly ascending by InstrumentId; duplicates and any non-ascending vector are rejected
canonical_order.listing_states: ascending by (recorded_at, instrument_id, venue discriminant, symbol, valid_from, valid_to), with null valid_to before a present date
canonical_order.listing_state_validation: the stored vector must already equal its canonical sort; a non-canonical vector is rejected rather than sorted silently
canonical_order.duplicate_rule: two listing states with the same (instrument_id, venue, valid_from, recorded_at) are rejected, whether equal or conflicting
canonical_order.tie_reason: The duplicate rule removes the only case where vector order could decide which listing state wins. The final valid_from/valid_to tie-breaks only make an otherwise ambiguous order deterministic; from the first durable revision the order is fixed.

frozen_rules: Each published snapshot contains the full instrument universe and the accumulated listing-state history.
The head snapshot is the single accumulated-history source for Reference(t_valid, t_recorded).
Do not concatenate listing_states from every revision; later snapshots already carry earlier history and concatenation duplicates or resurrects stale records.
Old revisions remain retrievable by revision id and are immutable.
Reference(t_valid, t_recorded) selects the latest knowledge available by t_recorded for the listing interval valid at t_valid.
Historical queries use the listing states' full reference contract and never substitute the latest instrument master for historical knowledge.
Delisted, reopened, renamed and restated listings retain their previous knowledge states; a correction appends a new record and never rewrites an older one.
history_model.known_current_defect: ReferenceStore::reference() flat-maps listing_states from every revision. P1-04 implementation must change it to query the head snapshot only and add a regression test for no duplication and no stale resurrection after a later revision.
history_model.retention: No automatic revision or source deletion. Any future pruning is a separate reviewed decision.

validation.timing: Validation runs before archive publication and again after every decode, before a caller can observe the payload.
required_checks: Top-level provenance validates: supported schema, non-empty identities, 64-hex SHA-256.
Instruments are strictly ascending and unique, and each Instrument passes its domain validation.
No (venue, symbol) interval is claimed by two different instruments over overlapping valid time.
Every listing interval is well formed: valid_from <= valid_to when valid_to is present.
Every listing state's tick assignment passes domain validation, including complete monthly reference-close, schedule and calendar lineage.
Every monthly tick lineage hash resolves to retained archive bytes.
Calendar validation passes, including venue consistency, unique dates, chronological order and lineage.
Listing states are in canonical order and contain no duplicate (instrument_id, venue, valid_from, recorded_at) observation.
referenced source hashes resolve to a manifest entry and hash-correct bytes.
The semantic hash and payload checksum recompute correctly.
validation.failure_rule: Any failed check publishes nothing and returns an error naming the failed invariant.
validation.deserialization_rule: A successful parse is not validation.

source_archive.objects: one write-once {sha256}.src file per content digest under source-archive/

rules: At most one entry per sha256_hex; a conflicting duplicate digest is corruption.
Blank or malformed complete lines are corruption and fail closed.
Entries are never updated or removed by the store.

lock.writer_scope: exclusive lock around manifest read-check, object deduplication, object publication, manifest append and tail recovery
lock.reader_scope: shared lock for manifest reads, fetch and verification; if the platform cannot provide a shared lock, readers take the exclusive lock
lock.wait: bounded wait, 10 s by default; timeout returns an archive-busy error with no mutation
lock.platform_rule: Do not rely on a process-local mutex or on one process per archive root.

publication_order: Rename it to the content-addressed path.
Append the manifest entry and sync the manifest.
Only then is the source available to a publication transaction.

newline_commit_delimiter.rule: A manifest entry is committed only when its terminating newline is written and the manifest sync succeeds.
torn_tail_recovery: On open under the exclusive lock, if the manifest does not end with a newline, truncate at the last newline.
Discard the unterminated final fragment without parsing or repairing it.
Sync the manifest and the containing directory after truncation.
Read-only storage fails closed instead of repairing.
newline_commit_delimiter.complete_line_rule: A newline-terminated line must be a valid version-1 entry; it is never skipped or guessed.

source_archive.existing_object_without_entry: Verify the existing object's bytes against the expected SHA-256 before appending a manifest entry. A path existing on disk is not proof of content.
fetch: Require a manifest entry whose sha256_hex matches the requested digest.
Require the content-addressed object to exist.
Recompute SHA-256 over the bytes and require equality.
Require the byte count to equal the manifest entry.
Return bytes only after all checks; an unindexed object is never committed source data.
verify: Iterate every manifest entry and require object presence, byte count and SHA-256 equality.
Reject duplicate digest entries with conflicting metadata.
Report objects present without a manifest entry separately as crash residue; never return them from fetch.
A failure is an error, never a warning.
source_archive.dependency_direction: The revision database may refer to archived objects. The archive never depends on a revision row.
source_archive.orphan_rule: If the revision transaction fails after archive publication, the unreferenced object and manifest entry are permitted crash residue. A committed revision that references a missing or hash-wrong object is a verification failure. Cross-store verification may report objects no revision references, but that is not store corruption.

failure_semantics.required_result: No new revision or head change
Complete revision and head visible after reopen
Writer is poisoned; reopen and resolve by publication key
Publication rejected with a stale-parent error
Existing revision returned; no duplicate row
Verification fails; no partial snapshot returned
Open fails; no destructive downgrade or mutation
Apply the frozen tail-recovery rule, then continue

failure_semantics.failure: Archive corruption in a complete record

failure_semantics.required_result: No false success; uncertain commit resolved after reopen

backup_contents: a consistent SQLite database copy created with the SQLite online backup mechanism or VACUUM INTO
a copy of source-archive/manifest.jsonl and every referenced .src object
backup.json with format version, creation time, store and payload schema versions, head revision id, database SHA-256 and manifest SHA-256
rules: Never copy a live database file while WAL files may be active.
Take the backup under the archive lock so the manifest and copied objects agree.
Write to a temporary directory, sync it, then rename into backups/.
restore: Restore into a temporary location, never directly over a live store.
Open the restored database, verify schema versions, head and the contiguous parent chain.
Recompute every payload checksum and semantic hash.
Run archive verify and resolve every source reference in every revision.
Swap into place only after all checks pass; a failed restore leaves the existing store untouched.
backup_restore.evidence_rule: Disaster recovery may be claimed only after a restore test proves a complete store and all references.

schema_evolution.open_rule: Open succeeds only for exactly the supported store and payload schema versions.
schema_evolution.newer_schema: A newer unsupported version fails open without modifying the database, archive or backups.
schema_evolution.migration_rule: P1-04 ships initial creation only. Any future migration is a separate reviewed change with backup and restore evidence; it may add tables or columns but never rewrites a published revision payload.

verification_plan.rule: A cargo test pass alone is not completion evidence. Each group must produce an executable test and recorded evidence for the implementation change.

groups.required_test: Persist, close, reopen and compare the complete snapshot, including provenance, reconciliation, calendar and listing history.
Revision ids, zero-based contiguity and parent relationships survive restart and reopen.
Semantic snapshot hash and payload checksum remain stable across restart; a changed payload fails the checksum; a changed semantic field changes the semantic hash.
Reference(t_valid, t_recorded) returns identical results before and after restart for historical, current and late-known cases.
Listing open, close, rename, relisting and late correction each append knowledge states; the head-history query neither duplicates records nor resurrects a stale open interval.
Every provenance and monthly tick lineage hash resolves to archived bytes after restart and after restore.
Competing processes cannot publish duplicate or stale revisions; the loser gets a stale-parent or publication-key resolution.
Kill a writer at each publication boundary: before archive, after archive, during the transaction, after insert before commit and after commit before return.
ENOSPC, read-only path, permission failure, lock contention and archive-busy timeout produce explicit errors and no false success.
Altered payload, broken checksum, missing source, malformed complete manifest line and conflicting duplicate digest fail closed; a torn final manifest fragment is recovered by truncation.
Restore a complete database-plus-archive backup and verify all revisions, hashes, head, parent chain and source references.

Measure representative full NSE CM and BSE equity snapshots: source revision, hardware, dataset hash, payload size, write time, reopen time, query time and disk growth. Set thresholds only after the baseline exists.

design_change_forbidden: SQLite dependency or Cargo lock change
Test files for the unimplemented storage behavior
implementation_gate.after_merge: Implement P1-04 in a separate change against the merged contract. Keep the producer-manifest provenance follow-up from PR #62 separate.

known_defects_to_fix_in_implementation: ReferenceStore::reference() concatenates listing states from every revision instead of querying the head snapshot.
ReferenceSnapshot::validate() does not reject a non-canonical instrument vector.
snapshot_hash() hashes listing-state provenance while its comment says provenance is excluded.
snapshot_hash_of() uses unwrap_or_default, which could hash empty bytes after a serialization failure.
SourceArchive uses a process-local mutex, not a per-root cross-process lock.
SourceArchive::fetch() does not require a manifest entry.
ReferenceSnapshot, Listing and ListingStateRecord are Serialize-only and need deliberate versioned decoding.
